notes: Measured assertions are checked by the same audit script the skill ships, so they favour pages built with it. They are objective (WCAG contrast, overflow, counts of sizes and radii) but they are not independent evidence of design quality; see blind-judging.md for that.
Never discriminating: horizontal overflow, document basics, labelled controls and runtime errors passed in every run with or without the skill. The model already gets these right.
Always discriminating on the two larger pages: text contrast, type-scale size, radius count and tap targets. The baseline landing page used 23 font sizes and 10 radii; the skill version used 5 and 2.

Cost: skill runs took about 1.9x the wall-clock time (269s vs 143s) and about 1.6x the dollars ($2.06 vs $1.32 mean). The token column counts cached re-reads on every turn, so it overstates the difference.
One run per configuration. Treat the pass rates as indicative, not as a measured effect size.
